title: One Sink
subject: two people sharing one small bathroom sink every morning in a new flat
caption: Piano-led indie pop-rock in the 2025 alternative-radio crossover style. An upright piano with felt-softened hammers playing steady quarter-note chords; live drums starting with brushes and growing to a full kit with crashes in the final chorus; a warm bass guitar entering on the first chorus; a reverb-washed electric guitar holding long notes. Intimate verses with audible room noise, a wide and loud final chorus, the piano always in front. Male voice, a soft close baritone in the verses, cracking up into falsetto in the chorus and turning raw and loud at the end. 84 BPM, E-flat major. Tender, amused and quietly sure. No trap drums, no autotune, no orchestral strings, no gospel choir, no EDM build.
lyrics:
[Intro - upright piano alone]

[Verse 1]
Seven-oh-five, the mirror's the size of a postcard
You lean left, I lean right, we take turns with the tap
You spit, I rinse, we've got it down to a rhythm
Toothpaste on your chin and you won't let me tell you

[Pre-Chorus]
Back in my old place I had two sinks and nobody

[Chorus]
One sink, two of us, elbows in the way
I'd rather bump into you than have the room all day
Fogged-up glass, you write your name in steam
One sink, and nowhere else I'd rather be

[Verse 2]
Your hair in the plughole, my razor on your shelf
You moved the soap again and I moved it back
We'll get a bigger place one day, you say it every Tuesday
I say sure, and we both know I'm lying

[Pre-Chorus]
Some mornings I pretend I'm late just to stand there longer

[Chorus - full band]
One sink, two of us, elbows in the way
I'd rather bump into you than have the room all day
Fogged-up glass, I write yes under your name
One sink, and I'm never moving again

[Outro - piano and brushes]
Seven-oh-six, you kiss me with a mouth full of mint
